title: Maths reference: Number
summary: The words and methods from Number Foundations, each with an example and, where it helps, a picture of the number line.
_about: Maths cards for maths/number (see snippets/maths.json for the format).

items.label: integer
items.hint: A whole number, zero, or a negative whole number.

items.label: negative number
items.hint: A number below zero, to the left of $0$ on a number line: five below zero.

items.label: less than, greater than
items.hint: The wide end of the sign faces the greater number. Further left on the line is less.
items.board:
widget: numberline
range: -10, 10
point A: -7
point B: -2
compare: A, B

items.label: further from zero
items.hint: The size of a number without its sign. Among negatives, the one further from zero is the lesser: $-10 < -1$.

items.label: mixed numeral
items.hint: A whole number and a fraction. A negative one is both parts below zero: one and a half below zero.

items.label: adding a negative
items.hint: Start at the first number. Adding a positive moves right; adding a negative moves left.
items.board:
widget: numberline
range: -10, 10
sum: a + b
slider a: -10, 10, 4
slider b: -10, 10, -6

items.label: subtracting
items.hint: Subtracting moves the opposite way to adding: subtracting a positive moves left, past zero if it has to.

items.label: subtracting a negative
items.hint: Adding $-3$ would move left 3, so subtracting it moves right 3. It gives the same as adding $3$.
items.board:
widget: numberline
range: -10, 10
sum: a - b
slider a: -10, 10, 5
slider b: -10, 10, -3
items.shows: Adding −3 would go left; subtracting it goes right 3, to 8

items.label: multiplying integers
items.hint: Same signs give a positive, different signs a negative. On the line: $a$ jumps of $b$; a negative number of jumps goes the opposite way.
items.board:
widget: numberline
range: -12, 12
labels: 2
product: a × b
slider a: -4, 4, -3
slider b: -4, 4, -2
items.shows: −3 jumps of −2 go the opposite way: to 6

items.label: dividing integers
items.hint: The same sign rule as multiplying, because dividing undoes it: check $3 \times (-4) = -12$.

items.label: placing a negative fraction
items.hint: Split each unit into equal parts and count from zero. A negative counts left, and the part counts further from zero, not back towards it.
items.board:
widget: numberline
range: -2, 2
fractions: 4
point A: -1.25
point B: -0.75
